summary: The Confederation of Sahel States declared in December 2024 that its territory is visa-free for all ECOWAS nationals. For other foreigners, the government's visa portal lists an entry visa or a permit, unless exempt, among the documents to present at the border; the UK and Canadian governments say their citizens need a visa. On 30 December 2025 the government announced it would apply equivalent visa measures to US nationals, in reciprocity for the US decision to place Burkina Faso under full visa restrictions. The UK and Canadian governments advise against all travel to Burkina Faso because of the threat of terrorism and kidnapping and the unstable political situation.

tips.text: The UK and Canadian governments both advise against all travel to Burkina Faso because of the threat of terrorism and kidnapping and the unstable political situation.

The UK Foreign Office says attacks on major roads and transport routes by terrorists are increasing, including through the use of landmines and other explosive devices, particularly where terrorist groups operate and near border areas. Canada's travel advice adds that improvised explosive devices pose a real threat on the roads outside Ouagadougou.
The UK FCDO says that to pass border control in Burkina Faso you must have a certificate to prove you've had a yellow fever vaccination.

The government's visa portal lists FCFA 66,000 for a tourist visa and requires a booking of at least three nights at a Burkinabè hotel; short-stay visa applicants must also provide a health insurance certificate covering the stay and a medical certificate. The Minister of Security said in September 2025 that nationals of African countries will pay nothing for visa fees, and that this does not mean exemption from the visa.

Canada's travel advice says most transactions in Burkina Faso are made in cash and to bring small bills, as it can be difficult to get change; credit cards are accepted in some businesses in Ouagadougou, but outside the capital their use is very limited.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Burkina Faso?
faq.answer: The Confederation of Sahel States declared on 14 December 2024 that its territory is visa-free for all ECOWAS nationals, and the treaty establishing the Confederation commits its states to promote the integration of peoples by facilitating the free movement of persons and the right of residence and establishment within the confederal area. For other foreigners, the government's visa portal lists an entry visa or a permit, unless exempt, among the documents to present at the border; the UK and Canadian governments say their citizens need a visa, and the UK tells UK residents to apply online or through the Embassy of Burkina Faso in Brussels. On 30 December 2025 the government announced that it would apply equivalent visa measures to US nationals, in reciprocity for the US decision to place Burkina Faso under full visa restrictions.

faq.question: Is Burkina Faso safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK and Canadian governments both advise against all travel to Burkina Faso because of the threat of terrorism and kidnapping and the unstable political situation.

faq.question: Does Burkina Faso have an eVisa?
faq.answer: Yes. The Ministry of Security's portal visaburkina.bf links to an eVisa application form, and the UK FCDO tells UK residents to apply online or through the Embassy of Burkina Faso in Brussels.

faq.question: Is the yellow fever vaccine mandatory for Burkina Faso?
faq.answer: Yes. WHO's country list says proof of vaccination against yellow fever is required for all travellers aged 9 months or over, and the UK government says you must have a yellow fever vaccination certificate to pass border control.

faq.question: Can ECOWAS citizens enter Burkina Faso without a visa?
faq.answer: Yes. The Confederation of Sahel States declared on 14 December 2024 that its territory is visa-free for all ECOWAS nationals, who have the right to enter, move about, reside, settle and leave in compliance with the national texts in force. No official source we could read states a stay limit.

entryRequirements.customs.currencyLimits.text: Est fixé à cinq millions (5.000.000) de francs CFA, le seuil à partir duquel toute personne, en provenance d'un Etat tiers qui entre sur le territoire d'un Etat membre de l'UMOA ou qui quitte celui-ci à destination d'un Etat tiers, est tenue d'effectuer, au moment de l'entrée ou de la sortie, une déclaration de transport physique d'espèces et instruments négociables au porteur auprès de l'Administration des Douanes au point d'entrée ou de sortie du territoire.

countryFacts.payments.text: Most transactions in Burkina Faso are made in cash. Bring small bills for payments, as it can be difficult to get change for your transactions.
ATMs are available in major cities where you can withdraw CFA francs.
Euros and US dollars are also accepted in some establishments.
Credit cards are accepted in some businesses in Ouagadougou, but outside the capital, their use is very limited.

countryFacts.safety.text: FCDO advises against all travel to Burkina Faso. This is due to the threat of terrorist attacks and terrorist kidnap, and the unstable political situation in the country.
Avoid all travel to Burkina Faso due to the threat of terrorism, the risk of kidnapping, and the unstable political situation.
Further attacks are highly likely, particularly in areas controlled by terrorist groups.
Kidnappings by criminal and terrorist groups, as well as by members of the country's de facto authorities, occur regularly.
A state of emergency is in effect in eight regions:

Attacks on major roads and transport routes by terrorists are increasing, including through the use of landmines and other explosive devices. This is particularly the case in areas where terrorist groups are operational and near border areas.

countryFacts.bestTimeToVisit.text: The rainy season extends from June to October. Seasonal flooding can hamper overland travel and reduce the provision of essential services, including in the capital, Ouagadougou. Mudslides and landslides may damage roads and bridges, which may quickly become impassable.

Pour le compte du ministère de la Sécurité, le Conseil a adopté un rapport additif à la loi des finances rectificative pour l’exécution du budget exercice 2025 relatif à l’institution de la gratuité des visas au profit des ressortissants des pays africains.

« Désormais tout ressortissant d’un pays africain désirant se rendre au Burkina Faso ne déboursera aucune somme pour s’acquitter des frais de visa », dit le ministre qui précise que la gratuité ne signifie pas exemption de visa.
